methods.label: Subtract the corner cutouts
methods.explanation:
Folding changes the shape of the cardboard but preserves its area. Every remaining part of one side of the sheet becomes either the bottom or a wall of the box, so we can find the interior area before folding.

The original sheet has area \(20\times30=600\) square units. Each removed corner has area \(5\times5=25\) square units, and the four corners do not overlap. Therefore the interior surface area is
\[
600-4\times25=500
\]
square units, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses rectangle and square areas and preservation of area when cardboard is folded.

methods.label: Add the five interior faces
methods.explanation:
The \(5\)-unit strips along the edges become the walls, so the box has height \(5\). Removing a strip from both ends of each dimension leaves a base measuring
\[
20-2\times5=10,\qquad 30-2\times5=20.
\]
The bottom has area \(10\times20=200\). Two walls each have area \(20\times5=100\), and the other two each have area \(10\times5=50\). These are all five interior faces; the box has no top. Their total area is
\[
200+2\times100+2\times50=500
\]
square units, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary spatial reasoning to identify the bottom and four walls, then adds their rectangular areas.
